title: I've built a full studio using ai, including a coding app to teach myself and others computer science
author: DuchessCupcakeGames
selftext:
I’ve spent the last few months building an entire indie game/dev studio almost entirely with AI tools, and honestly it’s been kind of surreal seeing how far it’s gotten since I started in mid February.

I had a general understanding of computer science and some HTML background before this, but no real software engineering experience. Most of what I’ve learned has come directly from building things.

What originally kicked this all off was building a chess app. That project ended up landing me a side job teaching chess in after-school programs, which was a pretty wild moment because it made me realize I’d indirectly made money from building software. That was kind of the turning point where I started thinking, “maybe I can actually do this.”

Since then I’ve made card games, creative tools, AI-assisted workflows, and now a browser-based coding/learning platform called Duchess Cupcake Academy.

The biggest thing I’ve learned is that using AI well is its own skill.

I use ChatGPT and Claude constantly, not just for raw code generation, but for:

\- structuring projects

\- planning architecture

\- debugging

\- refactoring

\- organizing workflows

\- explaining concepts I don’t fully understand yet

\- rewriting prompts until the outputs stop looking like spaghetti

One thing people don’t really talk about enough is how bad prompting can create technical debt FAST. Early on I was brute forcing things and burning through credits. Over time I got way better at writing structured specs and cleaner prompts so the projects stay coherent and scalable.

As the projects got bigger, I realized I had knowledge gaps in stuff like git, terminal workflows, algorithms, software architecture, and deeper CS fundamentals. Instead of stopping to go follow tutorials somewhere else, I decided to build my own learning platform around how I personally learn best.

So Duchess Cupcake Academy turned into this weird hybrid of:

\- interactive coding lessons

\- browser coding labs

\- terminal simulations

\- game dev courses

\- music production lessons

\- AI workflow tutorials

\- built-in tools with no setup required

Ironically, using AI heavily has made me MORE interested in understanding programming fundamentals, not less. The better I understand what’s happening under the hood, the better my prompts, debugging, and decision making become.

It honestly feels like we’re entering a new era where “learning to code” and “learning to direct AI” are becoming intertwined skills.

Curious how many other people here are building this way too.

replies.author: DuchessCupcakeGames
replies.body: Yes, you can just ask ai, but what if you don't know what questions to ask? Why does anyone take courses in anything? It's structured learning with a database of resources. I created it as a personal learning tool for myself and thought it might be useful for vibe coders that don't know what they are doing and are just blindly asking questions down rabbit holes. I get it that but everyone learns the same way, but if you're the kind of hands on learner like me, you might want a structured curriculum like this.
